translation_notes: OWL_NS = Namespace('http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#') absorbed into '@prefix owl: <...> .'; the four namespace terms become prefixed names: OWL_NS.intersectionOf/OWL_NS.unionOf inside a list literal (an operand context, so the islands are recognised), RDFS.label and RDFS.comment in call-argument position

the mechanical draft named the prefix after the Python variable (owl-ns:), which is unusable outside g{} islands, and inserted the @prefix statements INSIDE the parenthesised 'from rdflib import (...)' list; both fixed by hand
only the prefixes actually used are declared; the draft also declared rdf: (unused in this region) merely because RDF is in the import list

context shim: infixowl_shim re-exports CastClass, Class, classOrIdentifier and manchesterSyntax from rdflib.extras.infixowl (rdflib 7.2.1), the maintained descendant of the vendored rdflib 3.x copy the region comes from -- the vendored copy imports rdflib.py3compat and no longer loads; imported identically by both sides

finding: the region is a serialiser, so ~60 of its 64 lines are Python string plumbing that the notation has nothing to say about; only the 4 term constructions change. No triple is written, so no g{} island appears at all -- graph *reads* (triples_choices, objects) keep their Python call form, ldpy having no filtering island
